highlights: A broad sell-off on 16 Nov: the ASPI fell 1.32% (−291.81 points) to 21,732.37 and the S&P SL20 1.49%, on Rs 10.48bn turnover; Commercial Bank, Dialog, HNB, Tokyo Cement and LOLC Finance pulled the index down most, and foreigners were net sellers of Rs 13.18mn (Rs 28mn out of Cargills, Rs 9mn out of Dialog).

Hayleys' September quarter: revenue Rs 178.7bn (+28.9% year on year) and EPS Rs 5.02 (+57.8%); trailing P/E 10.2x and P/B 1.54x at Rs 236.25. HNB Stockbrokers rates it Moderate buy with a Rs 260 target, about 72% above this site's fair value of Rs 151 (buy below Rs 128).

The broker's 13 Nov recommendation table is far more optimistic than this site on most shared names: HNB target Rs 575 vs fair value Rs 351 (+64%), Commercial Bank Rs 253 vs Rs 182 (+39%), ACL Cables Rs 115 vs Rs 64.7 (+78%), Hemas Rs 39 vs Rs 16 (+144%), John Keells Rs 30 vs Rs 13.2 (+127%) and Access Engineering Rs 90 vs Rs 47 (+91%). Only Sampath agrees: target Rs 190 vs fair value Rs 186.

HNB Stockbrokers says Budget 2027's primary surplus just meets the IMF target but leaves little margin once the IMF programme ends; the 2027 borrowing plan has no international sovereign bond, relying on bilateral and multilateral loans.
Tourism earnings rose 3.5% year on year in October to $192.7mn on record monthly arrivals of 168,625, but the first ten months are still down 8.3% at $2.43bn.

news.title: Budget 2027 and borrowing
news.text: HNB Stockbrokers says the budget's primary surplus just meets the IMF target, but the margin for error narrows after the IMF programme ends and Sri Lanka returns to bond markets; continued fiscal discipline is key to rating upgrades, and the country's elevated term premium raises borrowing costs. The 2027 borrowing plan has no international sovereign bond, relying on bilateral and multilateral loans, though cheap concessional funding will shrink now that the World Bank classes Sri Lanka as upper-middle income.

news.title: Other local news
news.text: The Consumer Affairs Authority summoned LAUGFS Gas over its domestic gas price rise, but cannot take legal action unless domestic gas is placed under a maximum retail price. October tourism earnings rose 3.5% to $192.7mn on record arrivals of 168,625; January–October earnings fell 8.3% to $2.43bn. Seafood exporters back the budget and see annual exports reaching $680mn by 2030.

news.title: Global
news.text: Asian markets fell early on 16 Nov (Taiwan −3.90%, Kospi −2.66%, Nikkei −1.57%; Hang Seng +0.89%); the S&P 500 had closed 0.40% lower and the Dow 0.10% higher. The yen held near two-month lows (about 159.7 per dollar) after a surprise Japanese GDP contraction. US diesel fell below $6 a gallon, a two-month low, as geopolitical tensions eased and demand weakened.
